summary: Explains that by default a non-zero return code or module failure stops execution on that host while other hosts continue, and that Ansible offers tools to change this, for example treating non-zero as success or stopping all hosts on one failure.
questions: What does Ansible do when a task fails on one host?
Does a failure on one server stop the playbook for all servers?
Can I treat a non-zero exit code as success?

answer_card.title: Default failure behavior
answer_card.answer_md: When a command returns non-zero or a module fails, Ansible by default stops running tasks **on that host** and continues on the other hosts. You can change this: treat certain non-zero codes as success, ignore failures, or make a failure on one host stop execution on all hosts, using the error-handling keywords (`ignore_errors`, `failed_when`, `any_errors_fatal`, `max_fail_percentage`, blocks, etc.).
